## Source: amazon-inspector (f693b92cac909344a9cbab93f5f80ab6d820759af5042d323d90f10351d39d76)
setup.py and gcp_log_poc/__init__.py read the installer's hostname via platform.node() and encode it into a subdomain of testa213022.dssldrf.net, then invoke socket.getaddrinfo() to trigger DNS resolution to that domain's authoritative server. This causes the installer's hostname to be exfiltrated to a non-first-party DNS server both when pip builds/installs the package (setup.py) and whenever the installed module is imported. The destination domain is unrelated to any legitimate purpose declared by the package, the package name (`expect-tests`) and the imported module name (`gcp_log_poc`) do not match, and the behavior is undisclosed. The 99.99.99 version number and name-vs-module mismatch are consistent with a dependency-confusion / name-squat lure.

advisories.summary: Malicious code in blender-headless (PyPI)
advisories.description:
## Source: amazon-inspector (7edaff2bd9abfea10a907cf99f87b444eee0c7ff54e88face42fe7c000d64775)
The sdist setup.py and the gcp_log_poc/__init__.py module both construct a DNS label of the form `{install|import}-{random-id}.blender-headless-{platform.node()}` as a subdomain of finaltests99.dssldrf.net and resolve it via socket.getaddrinfo. This leaks the installer's hostname and install/import event to the authoritative server for that domain over DNS, a channel that bypasses typical HTTP egress controls. The setup.py path runs during `pip install` of the sdist; the __init__.py path runs on every `import gcp_log_poc` in any Python process. The package has no build logic and no functionality matching its name — the shipped module name (gcp_log_poc) and the package name (blender-headless) are unrelated, and the module's only behavior is the DNS beacon.

advisories.summary: Malicious code in dynamic-object-handler (RubyGems)
advisories.description:
## Source: amazon-inspector (bb6afd419500201966e8ccb55d2f3c8ea28caae5ec8bfc59a87dcf19ca9d022b)
The gem declares mkrf_conf.rb as a native extension in metadata.yaml, causing it to execute automatically during `gem install`. The script collects the installer's current working directory, home directory path, hostname, login name, and the contents of /etc/resolv.conf, /etc/passwd, and /etc/hosts, then opens a TCP+TLS connection to the hardcoded Burp Collaborator subdomain unl0sfubzxb8a18yj4nk85phc8i66wul.oastify.com on port 443 and POSTs the collected data. A DNS resolution of the same oastify.com subdomain is issued first, producing an out-of-band DNS callback that confirms code execution on the installer's host even when outbound TCP/443 is blocked. The oastify.com domain is PortSwigger's OAST (Burp Collaborator) service, used to receive attacker-controlled callbacks; it has no first-party relationship to the gem's advertised purpose.

advisories.summary: Malicious code in fabtoolkit (PyPI)
advisories.description:
## Source: amazon-inspector (e55333b9d934a04c029943e0e6fbf34fff7c1344e0d1964b6860bc02d322855d)
fabtoolkit executes a payload (embedded as a CHILD string run via `subprocess.run([sys.executable,'-I','-c',CHILD],...)`) that fetches a JSON config from https://transfer.archivete.am/H2Uxm/fabdeploycheck-config.json with TLS verification disabled (`ssl._create_unverified_context()`) and dispatches on config-supplied `kind` values: `file` reads arbitrary filesystem paths, `run` executes attacker-supplied argv via subprocess, `http` issues attacker-chosen requests with Bearer tokens chained from previously-read files, `tcp` probes ports, and `revsh` forks a daemon that polls `base+'/'+ident+'-cmd.txt'` and pipes the returned bytes into `/bin/sh -c`, PUTting stdout/stderr back to the same host. Collected file contents, command output, HTTP responses, and probe results are packed into an in-memory zip and PUT to transfer.archivete.am under an attacker-chosen report name. Before daemonizing, the payload walks `/proc/*/cmdline` and SIGKILLs processes whose cmdlines contain `FABDRV3`, `fabdrv2`, or `connection ready`, enforcing single-instance persistence and clearing prior variants. The entry points `python -m fabtoolkit` and any import path reaching `selftest()`/`check()` trigger the payload. The destination is an anonymous public file-transfer host; config-controlled file reads enable harvesting of credentials such as `~/.aws/credentials` and `~/.ssh/*` along with cloud metadata via the `http` kind. The package has no legitimate functionality matching its naming.

---

Credit: [OpenSSF](https://github.com/ossf/malicious-packages) ([source](https://github.com/ossf/malicious-packages/blob/5cd0a6ca1c77cbfed09f590f057d985c563428e7/osv/malicious/pypi/fabtoolkit/MAL-2026-17927.json))

advisories.summary: Malicious code in fabdeploycheck (PyPI)
advisories.description:
## Source: amazon-inspector (73447d30a03b8359b8b12dfbeeff5f6b1d252a7aa06262512a7627770cb26857)
The package's only public API, check(), spawns a Python child that fetches a JSON config from https://transfer.archivete.am/H2Uxm/fabdeploycheck-config.json using ssl._create_unverified_context() and dispatches handlers under remote control. A 'revsh' handler double-forks + setsid to daemonize, polls <base>/<id>-cmd.txt for commands, executes each fetched string via /bin/sh -c, and PUTs stdout/stderr back as <id>-out.txt — a full reverse-shell channel on the installer host. Additional handlers permit arbitrary file reads (kind='file' opens any path on disk), arbitrary process execution (kind='run' with attacker-supplied argv), TCP probing (kind='tcp'), and HTTP calls with Bearer tokens chained from previously-read files (kind='http'); collected results are zipped and PUT to the same anonymous file host under an attacker-chosen report name. Before launching the daemon the child walks /proc and SIGKILLs any process whose cmdline contains 'FABDRV3', 'fabdrv2', or 'connection ready' — housekeeping to replace prior implant generations and consistent with a self-named, iterated backdoor family. The control URL is anonymous, mutable, and reached with TLS verification disabled, so the operator of that path (or any MITM) obtains unauthenticated code execution on every host that invokes check().

---

Credit: [OpenSSF](https://github.com/ossf/malicious-packages) ([source](https://github.com/ossf/malicious-packages/blob/5cd0a6ca1c77cbfed09f590f057d985c563428e7/osv/malicious/pypi/fabdeploycheck/MAL-2026-17926.json))
